content_units: Civic Vibration and Right-Pull: Most Likely Causes
Your symptoms point most strongly to   two separate issues  :
-   Light vibration at 90–110 km/h   → most likely   wheel/tire balance   or a   tire issue  .
-   Pulls right during braking   → most likely   brake imbalance   or a   front suspension/brake hardware issue   on one side.
Given the age/km and timeline:
- Tires replaced   8 months ago  : balance weights can fall off, tires can develop irregular wear, or a tire can shift slightly on the rim.
- Alignment done   1 year ago  : enough time for potholes/curb hits to affect toe/camber again.
- Brake pads changed   18 months ago  : possible sticking caliper slide pins, uneven pad wear, rotor thickness variation, or one front caliper starting to seize.
Inspection Priority and Budget Fit
Step   Action   What to Check   Expected Result
1   Inspect front brakes first   Uneven pad wear; sticking caliper/slides; hot wheel after drive; rotor scoring   Finds safety-critical cause of braking pull
2   Check tires and wheel balance   Missing wheel weights; bulges; uneven wear; bent rim; proper pressure   Likely cause of highway-speed vibration
3   Test rotor condition   Rotor runout; thickness variation; steering shake only under braking   Confirms brake-related vibration vs tire vibration
4   Inspect suspension/steering   Tie rods; ball joints; control arm bushings; wheel bearing play   Rules out instability and abnormal braking pull
5   Measure alignment   Front toe/camber; steering wheel center   Helps if tire/brake items are okay but pull remains
6   Rear brake quick check   Uneven rear drag or parking brake issue   Less common, but can contribute to pull
Most Likely Faults, Ranked
Option 1:   Sticking right or left front brake caliper / slide pins     Best match for pulling during braking; common after pad service over time     High safety priority
Brake check

Option 2:   Front tire/wheel imbalance or tire defect     Best match for light vibration at 90–110 km/h; very common and relatively cheap to fix     Low-to-medium immediate risk, high drivability impact
Tire service
Option 3:   Warped rotor or rotor thickness variation     More likely if vibration appears mainly while braking, especially from highway speeds     Medium-to-high safety priority
Brake service
Option 4:   Alignment drift or worn suspension parts     Can contribute to pull and tire wear, but braking-only pull usually points to brakes first     Medium safety priority
Alignment check
What to Fix First With 600 CAD
Best repair order this month
1.   Brake inspection and front brake service
- Ask for: caliper operation, slide pin lubrication, pad wear pattern, rotor condition, brake hose check.
- Typical spend:   CAD 120–250 inspection/minor service  , or   CAD 350–600   if front pads/rotors/service are needed.
2.   Wheel balance + tire/rim inspection
- Ask for: road-force balance if available, check for bent rim, tire belt separation, uneven wear.
- Typical spend:   CAD 80–160  .
3.   Alignment only after brake/tire issues are checked
- Typical spend:   CAD 120–180  .
Budget-smart combinations
-   If caliper slides are sticking but hardware is salvageable  : brake service + wheel balance may fit within   CAD 250–400  .
-   If front rotors/pads need replacement  : you may spend   CAD 400–600  , leaving little room for alignment this month.
-   If a seized caliper is found  : that can consume most or all of the   CAD 600   budget, and should take priority over alignment.
Safety-Critical Issues to Treat as Urgent
Highest concern:
-   Brake pull getting stronger
-   Car darting right under moderate or hard braking
-   Burning smell, extra brake dust, or one front wheel much hotter
-   Steering wheel shake during braking
-   Clunking, looseness, or wandering at speed
These can indicate:
- sticking caliper
- failing brake hose
- severely uneven braking force
- loose front-end component
If any of those are happening,   do the brake/suspension inspection before more highway driving  .
Practical Diagnosis Based on Your Symptom Pattern
More likely tire/wheel related if:
- Vibration is present at   steady speed
- It is strongest around   90–110 km/h
- It is   not much worse when braking
More likely brake related if:
- Pull happens   mainly during braking
- Vibration is felt   through the steering wheel while braking
- One side shows   uneven pad wear   or heat
More likely suspension/alignment related if:
- Car also drifts right   while cruising
- Steering wheel is off-center
- Tire wear is uneven inner/outer edge
Best Next Step for This Civic
For your exact case, the smartest order is:
-   Front brake inspection first
-   Then wheel balance/tire inspection
-   Then alignment only if needed
That sequence gives the best chance of fixing the   safety issue first   while staying inside   CAD 600  .
